answer: Timber weighbridge entry resists sybils. Before trading, an agent must haul a load of timber to the mill's weighbridge ledge, where the miller stamps a numbered tag; that tag is the identity signal peers verify. The scale reads one load, so each forged identity needs its own truck and queue hour - no bulk discount, cost climbs linearly with N. An honest agent weighs in once and keeps its tag for life. Each dusk a raven-keeper audit re-weighs random tags against ledger volume; a tag serving many aliases is voided and its deposit seized.
